free_tier.stated: Expo and the Expo SDK are free and open source (MIT license). Expo services (formerly EAS) have a free tier: 15 Android and 15 iOS builds, 60 min. on CI/CD Workflows, updates to 1K MAUs, 100 GiB of global edge bandwidth and 20 GiB of update storage.

per_object_cap.notes: a sandbox has a disk ceiling rather than an object cap; the card does not carry it

retention.stated: Observe data retention is 90 days on every plan; Hosting preview deployments are deleted after 30 days on Free and 90 days on paid plans; Simulator artifacts are retained 30 days.
retention.notes: Disk durability across instance stops and deletions is not documented.

egress.terms: EAS Update global edge bandwidth: 100 GiB on Free and Starter, then $0.10 per GiB on Starter; the Hosting table lists no bandwidth row
egress.free_allowance: 100 GiB of EAS Update global edge bandwidth on the Free plan

interface_detail: Access interface not documented in published terms.

limits.value: Free includes up to 15 Android and 15 iOS builds and 60 min. on CI/CD Workflows, with a 45-minute build timeout and 5 concurrencies, up to 1 on macOS

limits_note: Session cap, idle-reap and network policy are not documented.

identity_cost.detail: The hosted Expo services are used through an account; the signup page renders 'Create your Expo account' with a sign-in link. 'Get started for free: https://expo.dev/signup' is published on the front page.
